verdict: RESPONSIVE ROOT CAUSE KNOWN — MORE EXPERIMENT NEEDED

rootCause.frozenBands: Only two deep observation viewports (1440 desktop / 390 mobile) + a 5-width geometry probe [390,768,1024,1440,1920]. The clone ships both subtrees switched at an inferred 915px midpoint; the mobile subtree receives ZERO inferred rules (generateLayoutCss hardcodes data-wr-viewport='desktop', src/reconstruction/layout-inference.ts:701) so 0-914.98px is frozen at 390px-resolved values, and the desktop subtree is frozen at 1440px-resolved values because authored fluid forms (fr/clamp/vw/%) are captured then discarded for resolved px; the fluid tier barely fires (3 usable samples, blockish-display gate, containing-block guards refuse grid/flex-basis items).
rootCause.pricing1100: The probe never samples between 1024 and 1440; the source's real switch is exactly 1025 (@media max-width:1024 hide-laptop / min-width:1025 show-laptop). hiddenRanges() interpolates per-node hidden bands to floored midpoints, emitting (min-width:1024px) and (max-width:1231.98px){display:none} for 503 nodes on /pricing — wrong at BOTH edges (clone also wrongly shows desktop content at 950-1023). Independent second cause: 1344px of frozen 1440-resolved grid track inside an 1100px viewport with no overflow management (250 chars offscreen even with the band removed). 1024 was already a BLOCKER at baseline.
rootCause.firstLossStage: observation (missing sample inside the 1024-1440 probe gap); the defect MATERIALIZES in reconstruction (hiddenRanges midpoint interpolation, layout-inference.ts:674,677-678); it SHIPS because layout-truth-check renders only at 1440 where the band can never apply, so all responsive-hidden rules are acceptedUnchecked (layout-truth-check.ts:46-51,107) — adjudicator-confirmed 738/738
rootCause.generatedRuleEvidence: app/public/wr/generated-styles.css:13541-13545: @media (min-width: 1024px) and (max-width: 1231.98px) { [data-wr-page="p000007"][data-wr-viewport="desktop"] [data-wr-node="n000359"] { display: none; } } — 738 @media blocks in the sheet, ALL at this single condition, 503 on /pricing; specificity (0,3,0) outranks the node's own style. Adjudicator recomputed the midpoint math character-for-character and reproduced the failure live.

sourceResponsive.notes: Source responsiveness is 100% declarative CSS (verified identical with JS disabled at all 5 widths; container rules exist only in video player/charts, not page layout). 'selectivelyPreservable: false' refers to RENDER-TIME rule replay: Strategy B preserved 621 genuine source rules and produced the worst result (regressed 1440, duplicate CTAs, surrenders asset independence). The INFORMATION is preservable and high-value at capture/IR time: authored breakpoints (1025) and fluid track lists (2fr repeat(4,1fr)) are recoverable — 30/81 linear sheets (8/8 stripe) are CORS-blocked from CSSOM but 100% recoverable by direct fetch; today authoredLayout reaches only 34/3254 linear nodes and 0/2280 stripe nodes.

A_extraObservation.note: Output identical in every measured field to a ten-line band clamp; more truth samples alone change nothing while the geometry tier is guard-gated and 700 < the 915 breakpoint. One indispensable piece survives: a single extra probe width near 1100 (fluid detection finds 508 nodes with it vs 9 without).

B_selectivePreservation.note: Regressed the one previously-exact width (1440: hide-laptop AND show-laptop both render), duplicated CTAs at 1100, requires build-time source stylesheet fetching + selector translation (shipped clone strips original classes — SiteSpec empties attributes), surrenders Task-22 asset independence.

C_minimalInference.note: Final AC5 form: hidden-band correction + width:auto-ONLY unfreeze (max-width:none destroyed authored caps — found by the Stripe check, confirmed on Linear) + px→fr conversion including single-track grids (the 1344px single track was the 1100 Enterprise pin) + 1100 probe width. 0 blockers at all 5 widths; 1100 offscreen 105→0; 1024 305→0 offscreen. Caveats (adjudicator): shipped bands end at 1061.98 = midpoint(1024,1100), not the claimed clamp — result depends on the probe sample; and everywhere the unfreeze acts it introduces one shared MAJOR-class signature (lost flex justification / row gaps: jammed logo row, nav cluster ~280px off at 1440 invisible to the clip metric, colliding cells at 1024, 4px toggle sliver) — the unfreeze must emit the frozen property SET coherently, which is the open experiment.

winner: C (minimal inference correction, AC5 form: corrected hidden bands + width:auto-only fluid unfreeze + complete px→fr track conversion + one extra probe width) — chosen after A and B were experimentally eliminated per the A>B>C preference order; NOT yet production-ready pending the coherent-property-set unfreeze, the untested mobile-subtree fix for 700, and authored-breakpoint capture
requiredWidthsNote: Final best variant AC5 per the independent PNG re-audit (baseline current: blockers at 1024 and 1100, major at 700). 1440's MAJOR is a REGRESSION from a currently-faithful width and is the reason the verdict is not READY TO IMPLEMENT.

stripeGeneralization.note: Zero code edits, zero selector-assumption failures; 1,906 nodes unfrozen, 78 grids converted; stripe 1100 BLOCKER→MAJOR. regression:false holds for the corrected (width:auto-only) form — the initial max-width:none form DID regress stripe 1440, which is how the mandatory correction was found. Band-clamp is a provable no-op on stripe (zero @media in its generated sheet). CORS trap and frozen-mobile-subtree residual both reproduced on stripe.

recommendedPrinciple.note: ADOPT NARROWED for responsive semantics, per the fresh adjudicator: PRESERVE as a capture/IR principle and as a constraint on inference (never infer an edge the source declares) — but NOT as a rendering principle (Strategy B refutes render-time rule replay). Plus a mandatory fourth clause: VERIFY — no responsive rule may ship without being rendered at the widths where it applies (today 738/738 responsive-hidden rules ship acceptedUnchecked).
